title: Auditable JSON shape instability detector and attribution
creator: Amit Varma
description: Build a production-grade, auditable pipeline that detects regressions in JSON response shapes and attributes them to recent model/config changes. The detector must be tolerant of benign schema evolution (optional fields added) while flagging regressions that break required shape/semantic constraints (missing keys, type mismatches, repeated nesting changes, enum drift). The system will combine field-level statistical baselines (presence rate, type distribution, token-length histograms), per-field model confidence signals, and sample-level structured-output validators to produce a single regressions score for each rollout cohort. Critical goals: 1) generate clear, actionable alerts that can be traced back to a model or config delta, 2) integrate with canary and A/B rollout plumbing to pause or roll back, 3) produce an auditable artifact (sample diffs + attribution heuristic + confidence traces) for postmortems and SOC/Compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented metrics for field-level presence and type distributions sent to metrics pipeline (Prometheus + clickhouse) for 10k request/day test tenant
Automated daily baseline job that consumes golden prompt set and computes stable per-field distributions; baseline snapshots stored with timestamp and model/config tag
Alert rule that triggers when weighted schema violation score > 0.12 for a canary cohort or > 0.05 for hosted-production over a 1-hour rolling window

End-to-end test: deploying a canary with a synthetic change that removes a required field must trigger an alert and create an auditable bundle containing 50 representative examples and attribution heuristics
Rollout integration: canary pause API invocation (console + control-plane) is exercised in staging with an on-call runbook
Dashboard: per-field spike charts, top-k affected prompts, and model/config attribution panel available in Console (read-only)
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with PM and Design; agreed scope to start with required-field and type-mismatch detection before tackling enum/context drift

2025-02-18: Prototype field presence collector implemented (worker + lightweight schema extractor). Collector emits presence/type counts to clickhouse table 'json_shape_v1' (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/1567).

2025-02-24: Spike: evaluated three scoring heuristics (KL divergence on tokenized field values, presence-drop rate, and JS schema-sat fraction). Chosen hybrid: presence-weighted KL + type-penalty because it balances sensitivity and false positives on optional field additions.
2025-02-28: Design review: security and audit requirements clarified (retain auditable bundles for 90 days encrypted with KMS). Action: add KMS key rotation test in staging.

2025-03-03: Integrated initial alert rule with Canary pipeline; simulated removal of 'billing.address.country' in canary to validate pause flow. Control-plane pause executed via https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/ and Runbook doc created: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X-audit-runbook
2025-03-05: Instrumentation PR merged for per-field confidence hooks (https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482). Next: add sample bundling + storage policy and PagerDuty alert mapping.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: strict schema enforcement causes noisy alerts during deliberate schema evolution; to mitigate we decided on a two-tier threshold with canary-sensitive thresholds and a gated 'schema-evolution' flag that requires a PM/design annotation. We will also avoid binary pass/fail on enums and instead surface top-k new enum values to the dashboard for triage. Performance tradeoffs: collecting full token-level histograms per field is expensive; we will sample and maintain exponential histograms for long fields. Auditing/retention: storing example bundles for 90 days increases storage costs; initial rollout will sample up to 200 examples per alert and compress bundles with zstd.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): collectors + baseline job + storage for snapshot artifacts
Phase 2 (2 sprints): scoring engine, alert rules, and canary integration (pause/rollback hooks)
Phase 3 (1 sprint): Console dashboards, runbook automation, and 90-day auditable bundle retention
Phase 4 (ongoing): tuning thresholds, extending to quantization/kernel attribution, and auto-suggesting rollback strategies
testing_plan: Unit tests for collectors and validators with synthetic golden prompts
Integration tests for canary pause flow in staging using synthetic failure deployments
Fuzz tests: random field drops and type swaps to validate alert precision/recall
Chaos test: run detector alongside heavy traffic workload to verify low telemetry overhead (<3% p50 tail latency impact)
follow_up_tasks: Add KMS rotation verification to staging pipelines
Map alert categories to PagerDuty escalation policies and Slack channels
Create lightweight client-side SDK for optional prompt tagging to improve per-customer attribution
Extend detector to capture enum/value-set drift and free-text semantic shifts
